en.21:1: As they approached Jerusalem and came to Bethphage on the Mount of Olives, Jesus sent out two disciples,
en.21:2: saying to them, “Go into the village ahead of you, and at once you will find a donkey tied there, with her colt beside her. Untie them and bring them to Me.
en.21:3: If anyone questions you, tell him that the Lord needs them, and he will send them right away.”
en.21:4: This took place to fulfill what was spoken through the prophet:
en.21:5: “Say to the Daughter of Zion, ‘See, your King comes to you, gentle and riding on a donkey, on a colt, the foal of a donkey.’”
en.21:6: So the disciples went and did as Jesus had directed them.
en.21:7: They brought the donkey and the colt and laid their cloaks on them, and Jesus sat on them.
en.21:8: A massive crowd spread their cloaks on the road, while others cut branches from the trees and spread them on the road.
en.21:9: The crowds that went ahead of Him and those that followed were shouting: “Hosanna to the Son of David!” “Blessed is He who comes in the name of the Lord!” “Hosanna in the highest!”
en.21:10: When Jesus had entered Jerusalem, the whole city was stirred and asked, “Who is this?”
en.21:11: The crowds replied, “This is Jesus, the prophet from Nazareth in Galilee.”

en.11:1: As they approached Jerusalem and came to Bethphage and Bethany at the Mount of Olives, Jesus sent out two of His disciples
en.11:2: and said to them, “Go into the village ahead of you, and as soon as you enter it, you will find a colt tied there, on which no one has ever sat. Untie it and bring it here.
en.11:3: If anyone asks, ‘Why are you doing this?’ tell him, ‘The Lord needs it and will return it shortly.’”
en.11:4: So they went and found the colt outside in the street, tied at a doorway. They untied it,
en.11:5: and some who were standing there asked, “Why are you untying the colt?”
en.11:6: The disciples answered as Jesus had instructed them, and the people gave them permission.
en.11:7: Then they led the colt to Jesus and threw their cloaks over it, and He sat on it.
en.11:8: Many in the crowd spread their cloaks on the road, while others spread branches they had cut from the fields.
en.11:9: The ones who went ahead and those who followed were shouting: “Hosanna!” “Blessed is He who comes in the name of the Lord!”
en.11:10: “Blessed is the coming kingdom of our father David!” “Hosanna in the highest!”
en.11:11: Then Jesus entered Jerusalem and went into the temple courts. He looked around at everything, but since it was already late, He went out to Bethany with the Twelve.

en.19:28: After Jesus had said this, He went on ahead, going up to Jerusalem.
en.19:29: As He approached Bethphage and Bethany at the Mount of Olives, He sent out two of His disciples,
en.19:30: saying, “Go into the village ahead of you, and as you enter it, you will find a colt tied there, on which no one has ever sat. Untie it and bring it here.
en.19:31: If anyone asks, ‘Why are you untying it?’ tell him, ‘The Lord needs it.’”
en.19:32: So those who were sent went out and found it just as Jesus had told them.
en.19:33: As they were untying the colt, its owners asked, “Why are you untying the colt?”
en.19:35: Then they led the colt to Jesus, threw their cloaks over it, and put Jesus on it.
en.19:36: As He rode along, the people spread their cloaks on the road.
en.19:37: And as He approached the descent from the Mount of Olives, the whole multitude of disciples began to praise God joyfully in a loud voice for all the miracles they had seen:
en.19:38: “Blessed is the King who comes in the name of the Lord!” “Peace in heaven and glory in the highest!”
en.19:39: But some of the Pharisees in the crowd said to Him, “Teacher, rebuke Your disciples!”
en.19:40: “I tell you,” He answered, “if they remain silent, the very stones will cry out.”

en.12:12: The next day the great crowd that had come to the feast heard that Jesus was coming to Jerusalem.
en.12:13: They took palm branches and went out to meet Him, shouting: “Hosanna!” “Blessed is He who comes in the name of the Lord!” “Blessed is the King of Israel!”
en.12:14: Finding a young donkey, Jesus sat on it, as it is written:
en.12:15: “Do not be afraid, O Daughter of Zion. See, your King is coming, seated on the colt of a donkey.”
en.12:16: At first His disciples did not understand these things, but after Jesus was glorified they remembered what had been done to Him, and they realized that these very things had also been written about Him.
en.12:17: Meanwhile, many people who had been with Jesus when He called Lazarus from the tomb and raised him from the dead continued to testify.
en.12:18: That is also why the crowd went out to meet Him, because they heard that He had performed this sign.
en.12:19: Then the Pharisees said to one another, “You can see that this is doing you no good. Look how the whole world has gone after Him!”
